objective_and_prior_variance.V32: Weighted pairwise logistic loss on positive-minus-negative differences, train-only weighted RMS scaling with1e-4floor, nonnegative L-BFGS-B coefficients and L2=.01. No intercept or probabilistic class-prior estimate. Predicts relative evidence margin, not a calibrated match posterior.
objective_and_prior_variance.V71: Baseline28coefficients remain frozen. The30residual coefficients fit pairwise logistic loss with the V32 baseline margin as an offset, nonnegative bounds and the sameL2=.01. Code and model metadata explicitly mark baseline_training_margin_in_sample_not_nested_oof=true: residual TRAIN margins use the outer V32 model that fitted those TRAIN query groups.
objective_and_prior_variance.V78_distinction: V78 already historically implements doubly purged inner baseline offsets but current V88/V99/V115/V134/V142 do not reference it. This is a known historical limitation, not a newly discovered experiment or a recommendation to replay V78 under another name. The V71 choice is not outer-label leakage in the residual fit by itself, but can bias offset margins/regularization. Do not describe the current residual as nested-offset calibrated.
objective_and_prior_variance.expressivity: Frozen baseline plus nonnegative residual can add support, not directly subtract a misleading baseline proof. Correlated parent/site/address interactions and sparse source coverage can redistribute coefficients; a zero coefficient does not prove a source has no information.
objective_and_prior_variance.variance_caution: The five models share most TRAIN groups. These standard deviations are descriptive coefficient dispersion, NOT independent repetitions, posterior variance, uncertainty intervals or evidence that a selected geography weight will improve recall. No prior/covariance uncertainty model is serialized.

monotonic_and_query_constant_claim_check.strict_monotonic_final_score: For a FIXED eligible candidate domain and identical tie policy, any strictly increasing f_q applied to the FINAL unified scalar score preserves pair order and top100 membership. Positive affine scaling is included. It cannot improve recall@100.
monotonic_and_query_constant_claim_check.query_constant: Adding b(q) equally to EVERY eligible candidate cancels from pair differences and preserves top100. Pairwise fitting cannot identify a query-only intercept. A query statistic can change ranking only through a candidate/view interaction or unequal source coverage.
monotonic_and_query_constant_claim_check.important_exceptions: Non-strict transforms can collapse unequal scores into ties; rounding/quantization can change ties. Adding a constant to only geographically/context-supported candidates is NOT a query-constant change. Adding a match-all branch can alter eligibility/short outputs, so unchanged-domain assumptions must be checked. A monotonic change to ONE component is not generally monotonic in the full score and may change ranking.
monotonic_and_query_constant_claim_check.tie_limit: Current scripts sort returned100 by(-score,SIRET) after Tantivy collection. This does not prove globally SIRET-ordered selection across more than100tied national documents. IDs are output/tie keys, never similarity features; report best/worst rank ties where exact attribution requires it.
